correctness.rationale: Surjective self-maps are permutations and, on a finite poset, order automorphisms; order-theoretic height/coheight preserves each two-point level, giving exactly 2^{n+1} homeomorphisms. For a proper image, if every occupied target level were full, incomparable preimages force levelwise paired images and the intervening-level order constraints propagate occupation across all levels, contradicting nonsurjectivity; hence some occupied target level is a singleton. Removing occupied levels toward that singleton by beat points contracts the image, so every nonhomeomorphism factors through a contractible finite subspace and is null-homotopic. Stong rigidity for a minimal finite space makes every homeomorphism a singleton homotopy class. The packaged enumeration for n=1,2,3 checks map counts, proper-image contractions and automorphism isolation but is not used for the universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: The published SCOPE theorem 'Self-homotopy classification of finite weak orders with at least three levels' already proves for W=A_1⊕...⊕A_h, h>=3 and |A_i|=r_i>=2, that |[W,W]|=1+prod_i(r_i^{r_i}-r_i), with one null class and a singleton class for each map preserving every level and nonconstant on every level. The assigned X_n for n>=2 is exactly the case h=n+1 and r_i=2, so the formula becomes 1+2^{n+1}; nonconstant self-functions of a two-point level are exactly its two permutations, hence the singleton maps are exactly the 2^{n+1} homeomorphisms. This covers the submitted final claim in full.

final_claim: For every n>=2, the canonical 2n+2-point minimal finite sphere X_n has one homotopy class containing every nonhomeomorphism and one singleton class for each of its 2^{n+1} homeomorphisms; hence |[X_n,X_n]|=1+2^{n+1}.
